Subject: Post-call: schema failover & validation matrix for Intellicorp integration

Thanks again for the call this morning, Samantha — good alignment on goals. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth:

1) Goal: integrate Redwood inference into Intellicorp's claims-extraction pipeline. Primary concerns you raised: guaranteed structured output (JSON), predictable latency, and graceful degradation when model generation violates schema.

2) Scope we discussed: SDK-based client embedding + reranking service, server-side validation of generated JSON, and a failover plan (re-rank / fall back to smaller model / canned extraction).

3) Action items (owners & rough ETA):
   - Dev (me): draft validation matrix and retry patterns (attached) — ETA: 24 hours
   - Marissa: propose constrained-decoding approach and sampling policy for canary — ETA: 48 hours
   - Jonas: audit auth + routing options (API key vs mTLS, regional routing) and cost tradeoffs — ETA: 48 hours

Attachment: intellicorp-requirements-v1.pdf (requirements you shared)
Attachment: validation-matrix-v1.xlsx (initial draft)

Notes on the technical approach (high level):
- SDK setup: we recommend using Redwood SDK v0.9+ with the streaming client; will provide a minimal example for server-side validation.
- Auth & routing: default to API keys for dev/test; recommend customer-managed mTLS for production Private deployments. Routing policy: primary to us-east Dedicated, fallback to us-west or a smaller-latency cheap model if SLOs are at risk.
- Structured output reliability: validate against a tight JSON schema server-side. If validation fails, attempt up to 2 constrained-decode retries (temperature=0, beam/avoid-sampling), then run a deterministic repair step (simple regex/structural fixes) before escalating to reranker + human review.

Please confirm the owners above and whether we should include legal/procurement in parallel (SLA/PII). Happy to jump on a quick follow-up tomorrow.

Thanks Dev — that looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Schema strictness: our downstream consumers expect the "claim" object with fields: id (uuid), text (string), confidence (float 0-1), and entities (array of {type, start, end}). If confidence missing, it breaks downstream aggregation pipelines. So server-side validation must enforce presence and types.
- Retry budget: we can afford one automated retry + one automated repair attempt before routing to human review (cost sensitivity).
- Embedding/reranker usage: we want the top-3 candidates scored by cosine similarity against our canonical examples; if the top scorer's confidence < 0.65, escalate to rerank + human.

I've uploaded a short internal doc with example inputs/outputs (see attachment). Also, can you include a column in the matrix for "idempotency key" and how retries are deduplicated?

Attachment: intellicorp-requirements-v1.pdf (internal doc)

Adding some technical guardrails and a proposed validation matrix. See attached spreadsheet — I sketched columns for: failure mode, detection method, automated repair, constrained-decode params, retry policy (count + backoff), idempotency approach, monitoring signal, and SLA impact. Highlights below: 

- Constrained-decoding strategy: use model-side decoding constraints where available (token-level forbidden lists for known-bad tokens and structural hints). For models that don't support token constraints, run 2 server-side constrained-decodes with temperature=0 and forced tokens for top-level keys.

- Validation and repair steps (ordered):
   1) JSON parse check (fast) — immediate reject + 1 retry with stricter args if parse fails.
   2) Schema validation against JSON Schema draft-07 — if a required field missing, attempt automated repair for common cases (e.g., confidence missing -> compute from token logits if available OR set to 0.5 and flag).
   3) Semantic validation using embedding reranker: compute embedding for candidate object text, compare to canonical set; if similarity low, attempt rerank with top-3 candidates, then fallback.

- Retry pattern: up to 2 automated attempts total. Backoff: immediate second attempt; if fails, schedule a rate-limited third attempt after 30s. Idempotency: require client-provided request_id; server stores request_id -> status for 24 hours.

- Observability: emit a validation_event with tags {account, model, schema_version, failure_code}. Create a dashboard for validation_failure_rate and time-to-first-success.

Attachment: validation-matrix-v1.xlsx (proposed matrix)

If this looks good, I can prepare a short canary plan: run 5k requests through Dedicated, monitor failure signals, and hold rollback threshold at 2% validation failures.

— Marissa
